label: rem:meson-mass-splitting
title: Meson mass splitting from q-deformed dynamics
html:
The q-deformation lifts the mass degeneracy of the meson octet. The eight states share the same hexagonal weight pattern but their masses split through the quantum dimension and crossing-energy formulas of the Hecke algebra.

The meson octet decomposition (\mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}) determines which states exist. The mass splitting of these states is a separate, q-dependent phenomenon governed by the Markov trace and the crossing energy.

q-independent structure. The weight lattice and the state assignments (which meson sits at which (I_3, Y)) are q-independent (Remark). The hexagonal pattern itself --- \pi^\pm at (\pm 1, 0), K^\pm at (\pm 1/2, \pm 1), \pi^0 and \eta at the origin --- is determined entirely by the Cartan matrix A_2, which the Hecke relation encodes independently of q.

q-dependent dynamics. Within the hexagonal pattern, the physical masses are governed by three q-dependent ingredients:

  1. Quantum dimensions: \dim_q(V_\lambda) = \prod_{\alpha > 0} [\langle \lambda + \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q / [\langle \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q. At q = 1 these reduce to the classical dimensions (all integer); at q \neq 1 they split.
  2. Crossing energy: \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}), the energy cost per crossing in the Hecke algebra. This governs the mass contribution from each braid crossing in the meson's knot representative.
  3. Markov trace weights: \tau_q(\beta) assigns a q-dependent amplitude to each braid \beta, producing the mass endomorphism via the Frobenius integral.

The Gell-Mann--Okubo mass formula. In standard \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} flavour physics, the meson masses obey the Gell-Mann--Okubo relation

  4 m_K^2 = 3 m_\eta^2 + m_\pi^2.

Gell-Mann--Okubo cannot test this. The relation is not something the framework should derive, and its \approx 6\% experimental deviation is not comparable with the \approx 3.3\% figure from the q-deformation of the adjoint quantum dimension.

First-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking means the mass operator is a singlet plus an octet piece transforming like \lambda_8, so that

  m^2(I, Y) \;=\; a \;+\; b\,Y \;+\; c\left(I(I+1) - \tfrac{Y^2}{4}\right)

for some constants a, b, c. Evaluated on the pseudoscalar octet --- \pi at (I,Y) = (1,0), K at (\tfrac12, \pm 1), \eta at (0,0) --- the Gell-Mann--Okubo combination collapses identically:

  4m_K^2 - 3m_\eta^2 - m_\pi^2 \;=\; 0
  \qquad\text{for \emph{all} } a, b, c .

This is proved over any commutative ring, together with the sharper consequence that two arbitrarily different breaking patterns give the same value of the combination, namely zero. In particular b --- the entire hypercharge dependence, which is the whole content of a breaking mechanism --- cancels .

Two consequences. First, if the QOU crossing-energy splitting is first-order octet then it reproduces Gell-Mann--Okubo automatically and exactly, and doing so is not evidence for the framework: every first-order octet model reproduces it equally well [gellmann1962, okubo1962]. Second, the only testable content is the \approx 6.4\% deviation, which measures the failure of first-order breaking through second-order operators and \eta--\eta' singlet mixing.

Second-order quantum Casimir curvature versus singlet mixing. An unconstrained second-order polynomial in (I(I+1), Y) surjects onto every scalar residual over \mathbb{Q}, so a second-order fit carries no separating power unless the operator is fixed in advance. Replacing the classical isospin Casimir by the parameter-free rational quantum Casimir d_q(I, Y) = [I]_q[I+1]_q - [Y/2]_q^2 [kleinkreisler1996] (which evaluates over any field without square roots to d_q(1,0) = q + q^{-1}, d_q(0,0) = 0, and d_q(\tfrac{1}{2}, \pm 1) = (q + q^{-1})/(q + 2 + q^{-1})) yields an (a, b, c)-independent ratio for M(I, Y) = a + b\,Y + c\,d_q(I, Y) (c \neq 0):

  \frac{4 M_K - 3 M_\eta - M_\pi}{M_\pi - M_\eta}
  \;=\;
  -\left(\frac{q - 1}{q + 1}\right)^{\!2}
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(q - q^{-1})^2}{([2]_q + 2)^2}.

At q_0, this bar-even ratio equals -2.7168 \times 10^{-3}. Because m_\pi^2 - m_\eta^2 < 0 on the pseudoscalar octet whereas m_\Sigma - m_\Lambda > 0 on the baryon octet, the same negative factor predicts the observed sign on both octets simultaneously (4m_K^2 - 3m_\eta^2 - m_\pi^2 > 0 and 2(m_N + m_\Xi) - 3m_\Lambda - m_\Sigma < 0). In magnitude, however, single-q_0 isospin curvature accounts for only 1.21\% of the observed 6.43\% isospin-averaged meson deviation (normalized ratio -0.2247) and 0.82\% of the -0.57\% baryon deviation (normalized ratio -0.3330), confirming that \eta--\eta' singlet mixing and higher-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking dominate the empirical residual.

The \approx 3.3\% figure is not a competing prediction. It is the q-deformation of \dim_q of the adjoint, a dimension rather than a mass splitting, and not a quantity that can appear on either side of the relation. Comparing the two numbers was a category error, and the comparison is withdrawn.

Ordered 3-strand gluon clasp for neutral flavours. Two-strand torus closures T(2, n) have vanishing hyperbolic volume and cannot distinguish an ordered constituent pair (n_1, n_2) from its swap (n_2, n_1) under symmetric content maps. Mapping the ordered antiquark--quark generation pair (n_1, n_2) \in \{3, 5, 7\}^2 to the parameter-free 3-strand gluon-clasp braid \beta_{\mathrm{clasp}}(n_1, n_2) = \sigma_1^{n_1}\sigma_2^{-n_2}\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1} \in B_3 gives \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) monodromy determinant 1 and trace 2 n_1 n_2 + n_1 + n_2 + 3 \in \{27, 41, 55, 63, 85, 115\} > 2 (strictly pseudo-Anosov across all nine generation pairs, while the real-substrate S^{(2,1)} trace at q_0 stays inside (-0.760, -0.291) near its q = 1 value -1). Although the 2 \times 2 S^{(2,1)} trace is symmetric under n_1 \leftrightarrow n_2, both the rank-2 (z_2) and rank-3 (z_3) full H_3(q) Markov traces separate \bar D^0 \mapsto (5, 3) from K^0 \mapsto (3, 5) by exact closed-form multiples of q^2 - q^{-2} (+0.2125 at z_2 and +0.1442 at z_3 for q = q_0).

Conditional on N = 3 and on Y. Mass splittings between isospin multiplets (for example \pi against K) depend on the hypercharge Y, which is open (the flavour-representations section). Within an isospin multiplet (for example K^+ against K^0), the splitting is purely electromagnetic and arises from the writhe difference, which is derived.
